outcome: Postmenstrual age (PMA) at first successful feeding (FSF)
Feeding performance (proficiency, efficiency, overall feed transfer)
cohort: Nineteen preterm infants (27-32 weeks gestation), including 9 with bronchopulmonary dysplasia and 10 without, from a level III neonatal unit.
finding: Infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) performed comparably well on paladai feeding (PF) to those without BPD, showing similar feeding performance and physiological changes.
followup_time: The last observations were taken at 40 +/- 2 weeks postmenstrual age.
cross-section timing: The study was performed from March through August 2012.
